findings.reason: The initial deferred-state implementation sends both entity and target to every diffed subscriber in fireDeferredSubscriptionDiff. Query subscriptions take only an entity; the official query-add test later received (entity, undefined) rather than (entity). Its last-params replay also lost earlier partial SoA values, although that separate problem was repaired later.

The initial buffer nullified a spawn found in any scope, and its executor treated an eagerly allocated but uninitialized spawn slot as an existing entity. Both cross-scope problems were repaired later. Its flushTopDeferredScope also removed the active updateEach scope without restoring it when an outer scope remained: commands deferred after an explicit flush inside that updateEach then enter the outer scope and need not execute at updateEach exit.

The subscription integration records wildcard pair removals but also records removeTraitFromEntity's base-relation-trait removal as a separate targetless onRemove event. The official wildcard-removal test observed three callbacks for two removed pairs, contrary to once-per-pair delivery. The exclusive-pair replacement path also retains a direct old-target callback outside this recording mechanism.

Wiring query add/remove notifications through noteOrFireQuerySubscriptions exposes the helper's incorrect diff behavior: its deferred removal path returns whenever pre is true, suppressing a real query-removal event, and the diff fires query callbacks with an additional undefined target. The official query-add test confirms the latter signature defect.

The updateEach rewrite inserted a second return results after the finally block, leaving a duplicated return and malformed indentation in the method. Step 122 removed the duplicate before final validation.

The complete deferred-state rewrite repeats the subscription-diff signature defect: fireDeferredSubscriptionDiff invokes every subscriber as sub(rec.entity, rec.target), including query subscribers, whose contract takes only an entity. This remained in the committed patch and caused the official query-add assertion to receive an extra undefined argument.

run_review.reason: The completed official evaluation is unresolved: 69/71 new tests passed, but a deferred query-add subscription received an extra undefined argument, and wildcard relation removal fired three onRemove callbacks instead of one for each of two removed pairs. Both violate the requested subscription behavior. The committed patch did pass all 128 existing tests.
